GOAL (step 5): add a minimal package-declared traversal contract. Containment alone does not establish a route; a connection does.
(A) Model: optional connections.yaml, a top-level 'connections' list, StoryPackage.connections default (). Connection fields: id (snake_case), from_place_id, to_place_id, via_id (optional world entity such as a fixed door, must exist in the world), access_fact_id (optional declared fact; absent means always open), consequences (optional tuple of fact assert/retract operations in the same shape other declarations use), arrival_text (non-empty). Reuse existing id patterns and strict-model base.
(B) Loader rejects, each with a StoryPackageError naming the connection id: non-mapping connections.yaml; duplicate ids; unknown from or to place; from == to; unknown via_id; unknown access fact; consequence on an undeclared fact; empty arrival_text.
(C) Runtime: storygame/runtime/traversal.py with a pure function resolve_traversal(package, facts, world, destination_id) returning a small frozen result (connection or None, refusal reason code). Legal only when the protagonist's current place equals the connection's from place OR is contained in it, a connection exists from there to exactly that destination_id, and its access fact (if any) is true. Refusal reasons are distinct codes: no_route (no declared connection from here to that destination, which covers unrelated known entities and places), access_closed (declared but fact false), already_there. A destination that is merely a known entity or a sibling in the containment tree is NOT a destination without a connection.
(D) Engine: add one public method on the engine (follow the naming of neighbouring public methods) that performs a traversal as ONE atomic accepted turn: on legal traversal, move the protagonist with world.place to the destination, apply the connection's consequences as story facts, append the arrival_text as a narration segment, then run the same post-turn sequence an accepted turn runs (record turn, advance and activate pacing, canonical events, authored transition, activation, incident-aware backstop) so that a traversal burns the incident window like any accepted action. On refusal return the engine's existing refusal turn type and change NOTHING (turn index, facts, fired events, protagonist place). Do not call the model provider. Do NOT wire free-text player input to it; a later step maps player language to a connection. Say in the notes how a later step could do that with the least code. Keep the engine diff under 80 lines and keep every scene without connections byte-identical in behavior.
(E) Fixture: extend tests/fixtures/stories/lighthouse-incident with a connections.yaml and any world places it needs (declare places in world.yaml following the existing style), one gated connection (access fact declared in the fixture's facts) and one ungated. Existing incident tests must keep passing.

TESTS in tests/test_traversal.py (each under a second, deterministic, no live worker, no billed model): (1) gated connection refuses with access_closed and changes nothing; after the access fact is asserted the same call arrives; (2) legal traversal arrives in one action: protagonist place updated, consequences true, arrival text in the returned segments, turn index advanced by exactly 1; (3) an unrelated known entity and a sibling place with no connection both refuse with no_route and change nothing; (4) already_there; (5) traversal burns the incident pressure event exactly like another accepted turn on the lighthouse fixture, and refusal does not; (6) save then restore after a traversal keeps the protagonist's new place and facts, with no second consequence; (7) loader rejection tests for every case in (B), built from a copy of the fixture in tmp_path; (8) a package without connections.yaml loads with connections == (). Reuse the existing save/restore helpers (grep tests for how other tests snapshot and restore).

HOW TO RUN: first confirm PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)" prints a path inside the cwd. Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov tests/test_traversal.py tests/test_incident_pressure.py tests/test_incident_engine.py tests/test_incident_loader.py tests/test_incident_characterization.py. Then the FULL suite: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider --no-cov -n auto (bare pytest, NOT with '.'). Ruff: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix <your files>, then -m ruff format <your files>. Do not run uv. Never use xfail or skip to hide a failure.

NOTES CONTRACT: step5-notes.md: one line per lettered item (A)-(E) saying what was done with file:line, one line per test (1)-(8), then the free-text wiring paragraph. Reply with a short summary.
